My take on Tower Semiconductor after Q2 2026. $TSEM Revenue came in at $460M, up 24% year over year and above the $455M the company guided. Gross profit was $138M against $80M last year. Operating profit $90M against $40M. Net profit $91M, EPS $0.80 basic and $0.79 diluted. What matters more than the growth is where the margin went. Gross margin moved from 21.5% to 29.9% in twelve months. Operating margin went from 10.7% to 19.6%. Revenue grew $88M year over year and gross profit grew $58M of that. So roughly two thirds of every new dollar drops straight to gross profit. That is operating leverage on a fixed cost base, and it is the whole reason this stock re-rated. The balance sheet is where I spend most of my time, so let me walk through it. Cash is $231M and short term deposits are $1,250M. Total liquidity $1.48bn, up from $1.15bn at the end of 2025. Total debt is only $142M, split $17M short term and $125M long term. Net cash is about $1.34bn. Debt to equity is under 5%. Equity is $3.07bn on $3.77bn of assets. Total liabilities jumped from $418M to $700M and at first glance that looks alarming. It is not debt. Customer advances went from $27M to $321M. Customers are paying Tower up front to reserve silicon photonics capacity. Tower is funding its expansion with its customers’ money at zero interest. That is a rare position for a foundry. The flip side is that this money is a delivery obligation. If Tower cannot deliver the capacity, the company itself says those prepayments can be repaid with penalties. So I read that $321M as both a strength signal and a commitment. Working capital improved while revenue was growing. Receivables fell from $223M to $203M and inventory fell from $257M to $244M, even with revenue up 24%. Demand is strong enough that nothing sits around. Days sales outstanding is roughly 40 days now against about 52 last year. That is clean growth, not channel stuffing. Property and equipment went from $1.46bn to $1.65bn. Capex in the first half was $343M. The company is deep into a $920M silicon photonics and silicon germanium program, targeted to be fully qualified in Q4 2026. Now the part I think most people miss. First half operating cash flow was $687M, but $283M of that was customer advances. Strip it out and it is about $404M against $343M of capex. Real free cash flow for six months is around $61M. In Q2 alone, $177M of operating cash against $187M of capex means free cash flow was slightly negative. This is a heavy investment phase, not a cash machine yet. Guidance for Q3 is $520M, up 31% year over year and 13% sequentially. Growth is accelerating, not fading. Silicon photonics went from a $180M annual run rate a year ago to $680M now, and management expects it to cross $1bn by Q4. There is $1.3bn of contracted silicon photonics revenue for 2027 and more than 70% of total capacity is reserved through 2028. The 2028 model was raised to $3.6bn revenue and $1.2bn net profit. That implies a 33% net margin. Today it is 20%. Aggressive, but with incremental margins running near two thirds it is not impossible. What worries me. Japan is a $3bn net investment after a $1bn government grant. That is more than double the current net cash and far beyond what free cash flow can fund. Tower will need debt, equity, or much bigger prepayments. That is the real risk sitting in this balance sheet. Tax is rising permanently too. The effective rate was 9% for 2025 and 14.7% this quarter, because the 7.5% preferred Israeli rate ended and the 15% global minimum applies from 2026. There is also the Intel New Mexico dispute in mediation, GlobalFoundries patent claims, and the Fab 3 lease case. The balance sheet itself has no weakness. The question is not solvency, it is whether the 2028 model lands and how the capital gets raised on the way there. At roughly $26bn of market cap the market is already assuming it works.

$IREN has officially completed its acquisition of Mirantis. This is more than just an acquisition—it’s a move from being an AI infrastructure provider to becoming a full AI cloud platform. By adding software capabilities like orchestration, monitoring, AI deployment tools, and enterprise support, IREN is expanding beyond GPUs and data centers to offer a complete stack. The deal also brings an established enterprise customer base and strengthens IREN’s position in the growing AI cloud market. While the acquisition comes with some dilution, it has the potential to improve margins, increase customer retention, and make the platform more valuable over the long term. If execution stays on track, this could be an important catalyst for the company.

Günaydın Güçlü bilançolar geldikçe önceden hedge için ödenen pahalı primlerin artık ödenmek istenmediğini görüyoruz. Hedging talebi azalıyor. Geçen hafta bilanço öncesinde hyperscaler hisselerinde gördüğümüz bullish küçük yatırımcı pozisyonlanmasının ardından, bu hisseler yükseldikçe perakende yatırımcılarda hem call overwriting hem de doğrudan put alımlarında artış gördük. Bu da temel olarak mevcut seviyelerden yukarı yönlü potansiyelin sınırlı olduğunu düşündürtüyor. Bugünkü AMD bilançosu öncesinde yüksek opsiyon satışı var zaten son bir ayda AMD’de ky nin açtığı işlemlerin yaklaşık %43’ü call/put satışlarından oluşuyor. IV %80 olunca herkes volatilitiden faydalanmaya çalışıyor. Anlaşılabilir bir durum.
